cards.sequence: Receive the wandering king; rule amid war; leave him to return after her death.
cards.attributes: Portrayal and defining behaviour are described in the sequence and distinction below.

cards.baselineRationale: Excellent match: Callidice protects another legendary attacker but never herself; the combat pattern makes her the ally whose fall preserves the continuing hero while ending her own arc.

cards.sequence: Disturb the earth; recover an old trace; make memory usable again.
cards.attributes: The past as a resource that must leave the graveyard of memory to matter.
cards.hooks: Graveyard departures store value; value recovers a permanent.
cards.assessment: A deliberate resource cycle needs finite costs, not automatic self-fuelling loops.
cards.name: Memory Beneath the Earth
cards.currentRules:
Whenever one or more permanent cards leave your graveyard, put a memory counter on this enchantment. This ability triggers only once each turn.
Remove three memory counters from this enchantment: Return target permanent card from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.baselineStoryElement: BG rare graveyard-resource engine.
cards.baselineRationale: The card rewards cards leaving the graveyard rather than just filling it, reinforcing the set's return architecture.
cards.sourceReview: Books XI and XXIV checked as memory pattern: knowledge of the dead and remembered kinship make the past actionable again.
cards.quoteStatus: source-led adaptation candidate; final card-space check pending

flavourCandidate.text: Memory becomes power only when something is willing to carry it back into use.
flavourCandidate.basis: Underworld memory and later family recognition treat the past as retrievable but costly.
flavourCandidate.fit: BG memory-cycle concept.

cards.sequence: Take the benches; coordinate effort; welcome another hand aboard.
cards.attributes: A crew becomes heroic only as a coordinated body; no single rower is the story.
cards.hooks: Crewing grows a worker; a completed attack recruits a sailor.
cards.assessment: The RW rare must build on sufficient cheap bodies, not just more Vehicles.
cards.name: All Hands as One
cards.currentRules:
Whenever one or more creatures you control crew a Vehicle, put a +1/+1 counter on up to one of those creatures. This ability triggers only once each turn.
At the beginning of your second main phase, if a Vehicle you control attacked this turn, create a 1/1 red and white Human Sailor creature token.
cards.baselineStoryElement: RW rare Vehicle/Survival engine.
cards.baselineRationale: The first trigger rewards crew labor; the second grows the crew after successful action, letting the card build its own future Vehicle support.
cards.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: crew-composite. Take the benches; coordinate effort; welcome another hand aboard.
cards.quoteStatus: source-led adaptation candidate; final card-space check pending

flavourCandidate.text: A crew becomes one body only after every hand accepts the rhythm.
flavourCandidate.basis: Coordinated rowing repeatedly determines whether the ship clears danger.
flavourCandidate.fit: Rare crew-composite payoff.

cards.sequence: Leave a possible route behind; land somewhere unknown; make it productive.
cards.attributes: Unrevealed possibility itself becomes a resource for the next landfall.
cards.hooks: Hidden bodies provide mana; manifestation enables land deployment.
cards.assessment: An original mechanical metaphor; do not claim the poem's strangers literally become mana sources.
cards.name: The Shore Beyond Sight
cards.currentRules:
Face-down creatures you control have "{T}: Add {G} or {U}."
Whenever you manifest fate for the first time each turn, you may put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield tapped.
cards.baselineStoryElement: GU rare Manifest Fate/permanents engine.
cards.baselineRationale: Face-down cards become provisional resources and each new fate can open actual land, making GU's permanent-heavy growth distinct from generic ramp.
cards.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: exploration-metaphor. Leave a possible route behind; land somewhere unknown; make it productive.

flavourCandidate.text: The shore beyond sight was already shaping the voyage before anyone could name it.
flavourCandidate.basis: Unknown shores structure the whole wandering sequence; the Manifest Fate engine is an original exploration metaphor.
flavourCandidate.fit: Odyssey-wide GU interpretation.

cards.sequence: Name the abused obligation; confront its beneficiary; exact repayment.
cards.attributes: Obligation enforced too late: material debt becomes inseparable from the moral abuse that created it.
cards.hooks: Removal; stored Food or Treasure creates an additional penalty.
cards.assessment: Keep context specific so every ordinary guest does not appear guilty merely for owning Food.
cards.name: No Debt Goes Unpaid
cards.currentRules: Destroy target creature. Its controller discards a card if they control a Food or Treasure.
cards.baselineStoryElement: Social order / hospitality, gifts and stored wealth create obligations; abusing those privileges makes the eventual reckoning materially harsher.
cards.baselineRationale: Clean rare removal carries an extra price specifically for decks visibly holding hospitality/wealth resources.
cards.sourceReview: Book XXII checked: Eurymachus offers material repayment for what the suitors consumed only after Odysseus has begun killing them.
cards.quoteStatus: source-led adaptation candidate; final card-space check pending

flavourCandidate.text: Restitution sounded generous only after the people who owed it had lost the power to refuse.
flavourCandidate.basis: Eurymachus offers to repay what the suitors consumed only after Antinous is dead and Odysseus controls the room.
flavourCandidate.fit: Debt/reckoning without endorsing vengeance as abstract morality.

cards.baselineStoryElement: Sailor knowledge / disciplined rhythm turns the effort of many tired bodies into speed, supplies and collective force.
cards.baselineRationale: A rare red engine makes tapping/crewing produce material momentum without requiring another named captain.

cards.sequence: Work the ground; expand the holding; sustain the household.

cards.assessment: The land-and-worker engine should stay distinct from the immortal tree or bed relic.

cards.currentRules: At the beginning of your end step, if a land entered under your control and a creature you control became tapped this turn, draw a card.
cards.baselineStoryElement: Rooted home / land and labor support one another; a household endures when people work the ground rather than merely possessing it.
cards.baselineRationale: Green gets a rare card-advantage engine that asks for both land development and actual creature work.
